content.text:
<challenge>
Create an unforgettable landing page for a fictional premium brand called **Elysian**.

Use these four images to shape the visual world of the experience:

- https://code.melvynx.dev/elysian-classical-surreal-still-life.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-greco-roman-scholarly-landscape.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-vibrant-mountain-river-valley.png
- https://codelynx.mlvcdn.com/uploads/2026-07-13/2026-07-13-golden-temple-starry-night.png

The experience should feel imaginative, editorial, luxurious, and slightly surreal. It should make a strong impression immediately and reveal more personality through interaction and movement.
</challenge>

<creative-freedom>
Always prioritize creativity. Make bold, unexpected decisions and develop an original concept rather than following familiar landing-page conventions.

You have complete creative freedom over the story, copy, layout, typography, colors, transitions, and interactions. Use the images in whatever way creates the strongest experience: crop them, layer them, sequence them, transform them, or make them part of the interaction.

Do not place the images into ordinary rectangular sections and call the page finished. Treat them as raw material for a coherent visual world. Avoid generic startup layouts and generic component-library aesthetics.
</creative-freedom>

<delivery>
Build the complete experience in the current repository. It must work beautifully on desktop and mobile.

Do not explain the design before building it. Make the creative decisions yourself and deliver the most original, polished result you can.
</delivery>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.

Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

content.text:
I built the Elysian landing page: a perfume house where each of your four images is a place sealed in a bottle. `pnpm build` passes with no console errors, and I checked every section in headless Chrome at desktop (1440×900) and mobile (390×844) sizes. The browser tab and the hero `<h1>` both read exactly "Claude Opus 5.5".

**How it plays, top to bottom:**
- **Loader:** the four images rise as vertical strips behind an "Elysian" wordmark and a 000→100 counter, then wipe away into the hero.
- **I · The Cabinet (hero):** the still life sits in teal-black darkness. A soft circle of light follows the cursor and shows the real colours, with a coordinate readout that tracks it. Press and hold to light the whole room. If the mouse goes idle, the light drifts by itself. On touch, a tap lights the room.
- **Doctrine:** a large serif statement whose words light up as you scroll. Small pill-shaped crops of the images sit inline between the words and stretch on hover.
- **II · The Academy:** a classical arch window, with "Margin" and "alia" on either side, is pinned while you scroll. It grows to full screen, the title halves slide apart, and a caption fades in.
- **Marquee:** a saffron band of the four perfume names that leans with your scroll speed.
- **The Four Vials:** on a light paper background, each image becomes the liquid inside a capsule bottle with a gold cap, and they fill from the bottom as you arrive. On desktop they tilt with the mouse; on mobile they're a swipeable row. Clicking a vial expands it into a full-screen page with the story, top/heart/base notes and price. "Next field" moves to the next perfume, and Escape closes it.
- **III · The Valley:** the river image is cut into vertical slices that fly in from above and below and lock into place.
- **IV · The Temple:** scrolling zooms through the temple's dark doorway while gold dust pours out of it and follows the cursor. Once you're "inside", there's a "Request an audience" email form. Its wax-seal button sends up a burst of particles.
- **Footer:** a huge "Elysian" filled with the valley image, which shifts as you scroll.

The stack is Vite with plain JS, GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis smooth scrolling. Fonts are Cormorant Garamond and Fragment Mono. I converted the images to JPEG in `public/img/`, so the page doesn't load them from the original URLs. The custom cursor and tilt are desktop-only, and heavy motion is reduced when the visitor's system asks for less motion. Run it with `pnpm dev`.

I left a headless-Chrome screenshot script and its scratch files in `.tmp/`, along with `puppeteer-core` as a dev dependency it uses. Delete both if you don't want them.
